Given that the differential equation 

$$
6\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-18y=24{e}^{-2x}
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{3x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $24{e}^{-2x},$ and ${e}^{-2x}$ is not a term in the complementary solution, so we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {e}^{-2x},
$$

where $\alpha $ is a constant that is to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-2\alpha {e}^{-2x}
$$

To find the value of $\alpha ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}6(-2\alpha {e}^{-2x})-18(\alpha {e}^{-2x}) & =24{e}^{-2x} \\ (-12-18)\alpha {e}^{-2x} & =24{e}^{-2x} \\ -30\alpha {e}^{-2x} & =24{e}^{-2x} \\ \alpha  & =-\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{4}{5}{e}^{-2x}.
$$
